messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

ASSAY TYPE: Droplet-Based Microfluidic Single-Cell Antibody-Secretion Binding Assay with Fluorescence-Activated Droplet Sorting (FADS)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Cell Suspension (mixture of antibody-secreting mouse 9E10 hybridoma cells and non-secreting K562 cells, ~1:10 ratio)
  - Bead/Detection-Antibody Reagent (6 um streptavidin-coated magnetic beads coated with biotinylated anti-mouse-Fc capture antibody, combined with a DyLight 488-labeled anti-mouse-F(ab)2 detection antibody)

STEPS:
1. Co-encapsulate single cells from the mixed cell suspension together with the capture-bead/detection-antibody reagent into 50-pl droplets, using a flow-focusing microfluidic junction.
2. Keep droplets cold (~4 C) during collection and handling to slow cellular metabolism and limit premature antibody secretion.
3. Shift the collected emulsion to 37 C, 5% CO2 for ~15 min to allow antibody secretion; secreted antibody is captured on the bead surface via the capture antibody and recruits the fluorescent detection antibody, concentrating fluorescence signal onto the bead in a wash-free sandwich format.
4. Re-inject the droplets into a sorting device and measure green fluorescence intensity of each droplet as it passes a laser detection point.
5. Sort droplets by fluorescence-activated dielectrophoresis: droplets with fluorescence above the sorting threshold (~1.5 relative fluorescence units, RFU) are diverted into the collection channel; droplets below threshold (background ~0.5 RFU) flow by default into the waste channel.

INTERPRETATION: A clearly distinguishable, bead-localized fluorescence spike indicates a droplet containing an antibody-secreting cell coencapsulated with a capture bead; droplets lacking a secreting cell (or lacking a bead) show diffuse, low fluorescence and are not sorted. In the reported experiment, sorting at the 1.5 RFU threshold produced ~220-fold enrichment of antibody-secreting (9E10) cells relative to non-secreting (K562) cells after a single round of sorting, confirming the assay's ability to isolate rare antibody-producing cells without any washing steps.

metadata.protocol_name: Single-Cell Analysis and Sorting Using Droplet-Based Microfluidics (Mazutis et al. 2013)

sources.title: Single-cell analysis and sorting using droplet-based microfluidics

metadata.notes: This is a much more elaborate protocol than most others in this set: the majority of the paper (photolithography mask design, SU-8 master fabrication, PDMS molding/soft lithography, microelectrode manufacture via solder injection, device surface treatment, cell culture/staining, optical alignment of the fluorescence detection system, droplet re-injection/spacing, dielectrophoretic sorting-junction hardware, and emulsion breaking) describes device fabrication, cell-culture maintenance, or hardware setup with no corresponding BioScript primitive and is a one-time/off-chip procedure rather than a per-run reagent-mixing workflow. The code captures only the core on-chip biochemical assay logic (paper Steps 68-92 / Section 'Cell encapsulation' through 'Analysis of sorted droplets'): co-encapsulation of cells with the bead/antibody reagent, cold-hold followed by a 37 C/15 min incubation to permit antibody secretion and capture, a single fluorescence read, and a threshold-based sort/waste decision. The sorting threshold (1.5 RFU) and background/detection threshold (0.5 RFU) are taken directly from the paper's Figure 5a; all other fabrication, hardware, and cell-culture steps are intentionally not modeled.

chemical_evidence.source_quote: we cultured cells in growth medium supplemented with OptiPrep and detected antibody
single beads coated with anti-mouse IgG antibodies in 50-pl droplets

operation_evidence.source_quote: single mouse hybridoma cells, a fluorescent probe and single beads coated with anti-mouse IgG antibodies
shifting the emulsion to 37 °C for ~15-30 min
the fluorescent probe becomes concentrated onto a bead, leading to a clearly distinguishable fluorescence spike
droplets having a fluorescence intensity three times higher than the background signal were sorted

numeric_mismatches.note: The paper keeps cells at 4 C throughout microfluidic handling (an indefinite hold, not a fixed 60 s), since BioScript requires a finite duration for the heat instruction, 60 s was used as a placeholder to represent the cold-hold step rather than a literal timed value from the text.

The 1.5 RFU sorting threshold and implied 0.5 RFU background/detection threshold are taken from Figure 5a; the actual instrument uses two distinct thresholds (detection vs. sorting) plus droplet-size gating, which are collapsed here into a single BioScript comparison since only one numeric threshold check is representable per 'if' condition.

numeric_mismatches.field: device fabrication and hardware setup omitted
numeric_mismatches.note: Photolithography, PDMS soft lithography, microelectrode manufacture, surface treatment, optical alignment, and the dielectrophoretic sorting-junction hardware are one-time device/instrument setup procedures, not per-sample reagent operations, and have no corresponding BioScript primitives; they are not modeled.

9E10/K562 cell culture maintenance, OptiPrep density matching, and CMRA staining (Steps 45-67) are cell-preparation steps performed off-chip before encapsulation; only the resulting 'cell_suspension' input is represented.
